_readme: Ground truth for retrieval evaluation. Run: python -m app.eval_retrieval
Each case is a plain-language question plus the section(s) that SHOULD come
back. A case passes if any expected key appears in the top-k hits.
Keys are 'act_key:section' exactly as statutes.py builds them - 'bns:103',
'coi:21'. Every section below was checked against the ingested JSON, so a
miss means retrieval failed, not that the section is absent.
Only BNS and the Constitution are ingested today. Add cases for other acts
as you ingest them, but never add an expected key you haven't verified -
an eval with wrong answers is worse than no eval.
'tier' separates the two things being measured:
citation - the user names the provision; near-100% is the bar
semantic - the user describes a situation; this is the real test

Cases for the acts ingested from mratanusarkar/Indian-Laws were added without being checked against the files - run `--verify` to confirm every expected section actually exists, and fix any that don't before trusting the score.
